rows.amal_said: شو يعني لسه الزباين يروحوا؟ ... لا، لا الزباين يروحوا. ... There are other words, but the one we know is لا.
rows.why: He used لسه (still/yet; sheet: 'still / yet | Lissa | لسه') for 'until'; Amal asked what he meant and gave la- as the word for until. Engine wrote 'divine' for الزباين (she echoed الزباين).

rows.chat: yoam el-5amees, wa7ad 3ashara alafain u sitte u 3eshreen
rows.why: For the date he opened with the feminine واحدة; Amal recast واحد and he then said اليوم الخميس واحد. At 02:55 he says 'So dates are واحد, times are واحدة', so he had not known the date form. Confidence is low because he also said واحد in the same turn, which may be a self-fix.
rows.r3_why: Amal voiced واحد right after his واحدة, and his 02:55 remark shows the date gender was new to him. Kept at low confidence because of the possible self-fix.

rows.why: Clock time takes the feminine number; Amal echoed واحد back, he fixed it ('times are واحدة') and she confirmed الساعة واحدة.
The sheet has 'morning | el-sube7 | الصبح'. صباح is the greeting/MSA form, and Amal's 'أووه' is not a fix. This is my reading, and it is unclear whether he meant a.m. at all.
rows.r3_why: Possible wrong form that she let pass. Kept as B at low confidence for Amal to review.

rows.medi_said: اليوم بلبس بلوزة، uh، أخ-أخ-أخضر أو،
rows.why: بلوزة is feminine; Amal's 'بلوزة شو؟' prompted him and he fixed it to خضرا ('it's feminine').
rows.english: Today I'm wearing a green blouse.

rows.medi_said: Uh, uh, حافظ، حافظ. ... لا، أنا نسيت، نسيت، نسيت.
rows.amal_said: Hafiz is a motivation، بس what's about motivated؟ ... متشـ... متشجع.
rows.why: He could not recall 'motivated' (offered حافظ = motivation, then 'I forgot'); Amal supplied متشجع - a didn't-know.

rows.medi_said: Is it-- Is there a verb for حساب? Do you guys use it?
rows.why: He asked for the verb 'to consider' and Amal supplied بحسب - a didn't-know.
He dropped the ت of متشجع (motivated) - مشجع is 'encourager / fan', a different form; Amal had just said متشجع and let it pass.
Amal's own frame was 'متشجع لـ العربي' / 'متشجع إله' - the adjective takes la-; he left the preposition out.

rows.medi_said: أنا في الـ Wi-Fi? Is that how you say it?
rows.amal_said: Yeah I'm on the wifi أنا عالـ wifi.
rows.why: 'On the wifi' takes 3ala, not fi; Amal recast أنا عالـ wifi.

rows.medi_said: So Shanteti, uh... Would it be El Shogol?
rows.amal_said: Yes, but what's work bag without any my or yours?
rows.why: In idafa the first word takes no possessive ending; Amal prompted and he fixed it to 'Shantet Shogoli, not Shanteti Shogoli'; she said صح.

rows.amal_said: That would mean is red. ... the adjective after it should be definitive as well.
rows.why: A possessed noun is definite so its adjective takes el-; Amal said 'Amra' makes it a sentence ('is red') and explained the rule.

rows.medi_said: So would it be شنتت، شنتت شغلي الأحمر، الأحمر،
rows.why: شنتة is feminine so the adjective must be الحمرا; Amal recast it immediately.

rows.amal_said: ما فيهن means there aren't here or there isn't here. ... Yeah, مشون.
rows.why: 'Not here' is مش + adverb; Amal explained ما فيهن means 'there aren't (in them)' and confirmed مش هون.

rows.amal_said: ليش؟ لا، ليش. ... It's just اسم. Why would it be feminine?
rows.why: He added the feminine idafa -t to اسم, which is masculine; Amal said لا and that اسم takes nothing.
rows.english: the name of his old school

rows.why: The first word of an idafa never takes el-; Amal said لا, and again at 30:21 when he asked 'So it's not الـ اسم'.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.medi_said: So الـ اسم قديم. No, it's like اسم القديمة. Okay, I don't know.
rows.amal_said: لا. [تضحك] لا. ... You just change the gender of Adeem.
rows.why: To make 'old' describe the name, the adjective goes masculine to agree with اسم; Amal said لا and told him to change the gender of قديم.
rows.english: the old name of his school

rows.chat: ma7al awa3iha el-mufaddal / ma7al el-awa3i el-mufadal 3indha
rows.why: He left out 'her'; Amal prompted 'But her' and gave محل أواعيها المفضل (owner ending on the last noun), and he then said محل أواعيها المفضل.

rows.amal_said: No. Even though in English we don't-- we say the, in Arabic we don't.
rows.why: Superlative أحسن + noun never takes el-; Amal said No and named the rule.

rows.amal_said: Mm, it works, yeah. هذا أحسن محل is like more efficient.
rows.why: محل is masculine so it takes هذا; he said هذي, Amal said 'it works' but her own versions use هذا.

rows.medi_said: No, not-- أس-- أس-- أسوأ الزبون.
rows.why: Superlative + noun takes no el- (the rule she had just named at 41:26 and 42:49); he said أسوأ الزبون twice and she did not voice the fix; chat has aswa2 zboon.

rows.medi_said: Okay. So أحسن الزبون ما، ما تشتري إشي.
rows.why: The task was 'the worst customer' and he had just said أسوأ; here he said أحسن (best), a different word, and Amal let it pass.
rows.english: The worst customer is the one who doesn't buy anything.

rows.medi_said: ما تشتري إشي. ما بتشتري. ما بتشتري.
rows.amal_said: It's ما بي، ما بيشتري because it's زبون.
rows.why: زبون is masculine so the verb is the he-form بيشتري; Amal corrected and gave the reason.

rows.amal_said: No, no. First you have to say the one ...
rows.why: After illi the verb needs the pointer ending; after Amal's 'No, no' he restarted and said اللي بحبه أكتر إشي, matching her chat illi ba7ebbo.
rows.english: the one I like the most

rows.why: He used هذا (this) for 'person / someone'; Amal recast أكثر حدا (sheet: 'someone | 7ada | حدا') at 46:20 and 46:43.
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.why: The verb needs the pointer ending back to the person; Amal recast بحبه and he said 'There's a pointer.'
rows.english: the person I like the most

rows.amal_said: Why? ... بس if you say the week's beginning, now you'd have to be إضافة which is two nouns, so أول has to be, like already has to be before أسبوع.
rows.why: He read Amal's الأسبوع الأول (noun + adjective) as an idafa, 'the week's beginning'. Amal asked why and explained that it means the first week, and at 53:51 she said 'صح. It would be the first week.'
rows.r3_why: A clear listening misread that Amal fixed out loud.

rows.medi_said: Il awal il tamreen or il tamreen il awal is the first exercise.
rows.right: awal tamreen / il tamreen il awal
rows.proposed_rule: awal / aa5er / taani before a noun never take el-: awal sayyaara = the first car; after the noun they are adjectives and take el-: el-usboo3 el-awal.
rows.why: Amal's rule this lesson: awal before the noun never takes el- (il awal il tamreen is not a form); she let it pass.
rows.r3_challenge: Amal answered 'Mm-hmm ... Of course' at 56:04/56:08 and voiced no fix. He may have meant the two options or been mis-transcribed. At most this is grammar-B, not a voiced correction, and it needs an audio check.

rows.why: He glossed tani ishi as 'something else'. Amal repeated it and said 'The second thing', and he then saw that ishi tani is 'something else' (sheet: 'something else | Eshi taani').
rows.r3_why: Amal voiced the correct gloss after his wrong one.

rows.amal_said: Nafs al ishi. ... نفس الـ إشي the same thing. نفس إشي doesn't mean anything.
rows.proposed_rule: nafs (same) is followed by an el- noun: nafs el-ishi = the same thing; nafs ishi is not a phrase.
rows.why: Amal recast نفس الـ إشي and said نفس إشي means nothing.
